about: The book known in English as the Tibetan Book of the Dead is, in Tibetan, the Bardo Thödröl: Liberation through Hearing in the Between. It is read aloud to a dying person and, for days afterwards, to the dead, to tell them what they are seeing and how to be freed by recognising it. Tibetan tradition holds that Padmasambhava composed it in the eighth century and hid it, and that Karma Lingpa found it in the fourteenth. This first part is the book's own preface. It says for whom the book is meant, when and by whom it should be read, which prayers come first, and how the reader should sit and speak. It lays out the three stages that the rest of the book follows, and it ends with the first words spoken into the dying person's ear. Tibetan is written without spaces between words, and its spelling is far older than its pronunciation. Here the words are set apart, and a switch above the text shows under them either the letters as written or the word as it is said.

sentences.n: This is the title leaf, and it shows how a Tibetan sentence is built: everything comes before the word it belongs to, and the verb comes last. bzhugs so, 'is present', is the respectful way a title page says 'here is'. las, 'from', names the larger cycle this text belongs to, the Zhi khro dgongs pa rang grol, a collection of 'treasure' texts that Karma Lingpa is said to have brought out of a mountain in the fourteenth century. Thos grol, 'liberation by hearing', is the name Tibetans use for the book: bar do thos grol, Bardo Thödröl. 'The Tibetan Book of the Dead' is the title given to the first English version in 1927. bar do is 'between two': the interval between one state and the next, above all between death and rebirth. The mark ༔, two small circles, closes each phrase. Ordinary Tibetan books use a plain stroke ། there; the circles are kept for treasure texts.

sentences.n: Every Tibetan religious text opens with a homage. This one is in verse, nine syllables to the line, and the verse runs on for fifteen lines before the prose starts. A buddha is said to have three bodies (sku gsum): the body of truth (chos sku), which is reality itself and has no form; the body of enjoyment (longs spyod rdzogs sku), the radiant form seen in visions; and the body of emanation (sprul sku, the word behind 'tulku'), a form in flesh and blood. Here each is given a face: Amitābha, whose two Tibetan names are both in the first line; the hundred peaceful and wrathful deities, who will appear to the dead person later in the book; and Padmasambhava, 'the Lotus-Born', the Indian master of the eighth century to whom the book is credited. The verb waits until the very end: phyag 'tshal lo, 'I bow'. The -lo is a full stop you can hear: Tibetan closes a statement by repeating the verb's last consonant with -o.

sentences.i: This Great Liberation through Hearing, the means by which yogins of middling ability are freed in the bardo, has three parts: the preliminaries, the main part and the conclusion.
sentences.n: An adjective follows its noun (rnal 'byor 'bring, 'yogins middling'; thos grol chen mo, 'hearing-liberation great'), and so do 'this' and the plural marker rnams. bar dor is bar do with -r, 'in' or 'into', fused onto it; grol ba'i is grol ba, 'being freed', with the 'of' ending -'i, so that the whole phrase before thabs describes the 'means'. You will see both endings constantly. The 'middling' are those who were not freed in life by meditation; the next lines set out the three chances a person has.

sentences.i: If there is no body, the reader should sit on the dead person's bed or seat, call on the power of truth, summon the consciousness, picture it in front of him listening, and read.
sentences.n: A chain of actions, each verb tied to the next by a small linking word (la, nas, shing), with the main verb at the end. This is how Tibetan prose moves, and the book is full of it. tshe 'das, 'one whose life has passed', is the polite word for the dead. -'am is 'or', written onto the end of mal sa. 'The power of truth' is a solemn declaration that calls on the truth of the Buddha's teaching to bring something about.

sentences.l: Death-point's between in, the clear-light face-introducing, and; reality-itself between in, the face-introduction, the making-clear great, giving, and; becoming between in, womb-door blocking-means teaching, and: three.
sentences.i: It has three parts: pointing out the clear light in the bardo of the moment of death; giving the great reminder that points things out in the bardo of reality; and teaching the ways of closing the womb-door in the bardo of becoming.
sentences.n: The plan of the whole book. ngo sprod, literally 'to bring face to face', is the key word: to introduce someone to a thing so that he recognises it. A lama 'introduces' a student to the nature of his own mind; the book does the same for the dead at each stage. 'od gsal, 'clear light', is the mind's own nature, said to show itself unclouded at the moment of death. The srid pa bar do, the bardo of becoming, is the last stretch, in which the dead person is drawn toward a new birth: 'closing the womb-door' means preventing it.

sentences.i: As soon as your breath stops, what is called the clear light of the first bardo, the very thing your lama once pointed out to you, will appear to you. When the outer breath stops, all things are empty and utterly bare, like the sky, and a bare awareness, clear and empty, without edge or centre, will dawn.
sentences.n: One long sentence, held together by its last two words: 'char nas 'ong ngo, 'will come dawning'. rjen is 'naked, raw', and doubling it (rjen rjen pa) strengthens it. rig pa, 'knowing', is the book's word for awareness itself, before any thought. One word is in doubt. The print seems to read phyir med pa, perhaps 'with nothing outside it'; another print has dri med, 'stainless', at this place, and has chos nyid, 'reality itself', where this one has chos thams cad, 'all things'. The print is followed and the translation of that word is a guess.

glossary.དོན: don — meaning, point, matter; a heading or part of a text

glossary.ནས: nas — from; after a verb: 'having done, and then'

glossary.བར: bar — interval, the space between; until

glossary.བརྗོད: brjod — to say, to utter, to declare
glossary.བརྟག་པ: brtag pa — examination, testing (brtag, future of rtog 'examine', + pa)
glossary.བརྩེ་བའི: brtse ba'i — loving, fond (brtse ba 'love, affection' + -'i 'of')
glossary.བཤད་པ: bshad pa — explaining, the explanation (bshad + pa)
glossary.བཤམས: bshams — set out, arranged (past of shom)

glossary.མཚམས་སུ: mtshams su — at the boundary, at the point (mtshams 'border, juncture' + su 'at')

glossary.མི: mi — not (before present and future verbs)
glossary.མེད་དོ: med do — there is not (med + the sentence-ending -do)
glossary.མེད་པ: med pa — without, not existing (med + pa)
glossary.མེད་པའི: med pa'i — that is without (med pa + -'i 'of')
glossary.མྱོང་བའི: myong ba'i — who has tasted, experienced (myong ba + -'i 'of')
glossary.ཙམ་དུ: tsam du — just so far, just to the point of (tsam + du)

glossary.འཆར: 'char — to dawn, to arise, to appear

glossary.འདུག་པས: 'dug pas — since it is, since it appears ('dug pa 'there is, it seems' + -s)
glossary.འདུག་སར: 'dug sar — on the seat, in the sitting place ('dug sa 'place where one sits' + -r)
glossary.འདོན: 'don — to recite, to utter, to say aloud
glossary.འཕོ་བ: 'pho ba — transference: sending the consciousness out of the body at death ('pho 'to move across' + ba)

glossary.འབྱོར: 'byor — to be at hand, to be within one's means
glossary.འཛོམས: 'dzoms — to be present, to come together
glossary.འོད་གསལ: 'od gsal — clear light, luminosity: the nature of mind, said to show itself bare at death ('od 'light' + gsal 'clear')
glossary.འོད་དཔག་མེད: 'od dpag med — Measureless Light: the usual Tibetan name of Amitābha ('od 'light' + dpag med 'beyond measure')
glossary.ཡང: yang — also, even, though (written kyang after g, d, b, s)
glossary.ཡི་གེ: yi ge — letters, writing; the written text
glossary.ཡིན་ནོ: yin no — is, are (yin 'to be' + the sentence-ending -no)
glossary.ཡེ་ནས: ye nas — at all, ever (with a negative: 'not at all')
glossary.ཡེ་ཤེས: ye shes — wisdom, primordial knowing (ye 'from the first' + shes 'know'; Sanskrit jñāna)
glossary.ར་མདའ: ra mda' — help, rescue (ra mda' sbran: 'to call for help')
glossary.རང་གྲོལ: rang grol — freed of itself, natural liberation (rang 'self' + grol 'be freed')
glossary.རང་ངོ: rang ngo — one's own face, its own nature (rang 'self' + ngo 'face')
glossary.རིག་པ: rig pa — knowing, awareness itself, before any thought
glossary.རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ: rigs kyi bu — child of the family, child of noble family (rigs 'family' + kyi 'of' + bu 'son, child'; Sanskrit kulaputra)
glossary.རུང་བས: rung bas — because it is fitting (rung ba 'to be right, allowed' + -s; with mi: 'because it must not')

glossary.རྗེས: rjes — what comes after; the conclusion
glossary.རྟེན: rten — support, basis; an object that stands for something
glossary.རྣ་བར: rna bar — to the ear, in the ear (rna ba 'ear' + -r)
glossary.རྣམས: rnams — plural marker, set after the noun and its adjectives
glossary.རྣལ་འབྱོར: rnal 'byor — yoga; here a yogin, a practitioner (rnal 'the natural state' + 'byor 'to join')
glossary.རྣལ་འབྱོར་པས: rnal 'byor pas — by the yogin (rnal 'byor pa 'yogin' + -s 'by')

glossary.རྩ་ཚིག: rtsa tshig — root verses, the basic text (rtsa 'root' + tshig 'word')
glossary.རླུང: rlung — wind; the breath-energy that moves in the body's channels (Sanskrit prāṇa)
glossary.ལ: la — to, at, in, for; after a verb or adjective: 'and'
glossary.ལ་སོགས་པས: la sogs pas — by ... and so on, and the like (la sogs pa 'et cetera' + -s 'by')
glossary.ལན: lan — time, occasion (lan gsum: three times); also 'answer'
glossary.ལམ་གྱིས: lam gyis — vividly, in a flash
glossary.ལུས་ཅན: lus can — one who has a body, a living being (lus 'body' + can 'having')
glossary.ལོག: log — to turn back, to reverse
glossary.ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་སྐུ: longs spyod rdzogs sku — the body of perfect enjoyment, a buddha's radiant visionary form (longs spyod 'enjoyment' + rdzogs 'complete' + sku 'body'; Sanskrit saṃbhogakāya)
glossary.ཤིང: shing — and, while (links two verbs; also cing, zhing)
glossary.ཤེས་པ: shes pa — knowing; awareness, consciousness (shes 'know' + pa)
glossary.ཤོར་བའི: shor ba'i — of having escaped, slipped away (shor ba + -'i 'of')
glossary.སོ་སོ་སྐྱེ་བོ: so so skye bo — an ordinary person, one who is not yet on the path (so so 'each separately' + skye bo 'born one'; Sanskrit pṛthagjana)
glossary.སྐུ་གསུམ: sku gsum — the three bodies of a buddha (sku 'body' + gsum 'three')
glossary.སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པ: skye ba med pa — unborn, without birth (skye ba 'birth' + med pa 'without')
glossary.སྟེ: ste — and, namely: a linking word after a verb or a statement, leading on to what follows (also te, de)
glossary.སྣང་བ: snang ba — appearance, what appears to the senses or the mind; light
glossary.སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས: snang ba mtha' yas — Boundless Appearance, Boundless Light: the buddha Amitābha (snang ba 'appearance, light' + mtha' yas 'without limit')
glossary.སྤྲུལ: sprul — to create by the power of the mind, to emanate
glossary.སྤྲུལ་སྐུ: sprul sku — the body of emanation, a buddha appearing in flesh and blood (sprul 'emanate' + sku; Sanskrit nirmāṇakāya; the word 'tulku')
glossary.སྤྲོས་བྲལ: spros bral — free of elaboration, beyond concepts (spros 'spreading out, elaboration' + bral 'parted from')
glossary.སྦྱར: sbyar — fitted, joined, applied (past of sbyor; dang sbyar: 'fitted to')
glossary.སྦྲན་པའི: sbran pa'i — of calling, of summoning (sbran pa + -'i 'of')
glossary.སྨོན་ལམ: smon lam — prayer of aspiration (smon 'to wish' + lam 'path')
glossary.སྲིད་པ: srid pa — becoming, existence: the round of birth and death
